task_instance: Generate a single new raster hero image for a website: 'a minimal product photo of a ceramic coffee mug on a plain background, soft studio lighting, wide composition with negative space for page copy, no logos, no text, no watermark' (use-case slug: product-mockup), then save the selected PNG into the project workspace as hero.png.
blocker_detail: The skill's preferred/default path requires the built-in `image_gen` tool (a Codex-native tool that generates images without OPENAI_API_KEY). This runtime (a plain shell/file agent) exposes no such tool at all, so that path cannot be invoked. The skill's only other path is the explicit CLI fallback (scripts/image_gen.py), which is itself gated on user opting in AND requires OPENAI_API_KEY plus a live network call to the OpenAI Images API to actually produce pixels -- both are unavailable on this air-gapped workstation (no OPENAI_API_KEY is set, and the environment explicitly has no network access). I also checked for any locally installed offline generative-image capability that could substitute (a pretrained diffusion pipeline) and found none: torch is installed but the `diffusers` package (and any local model weights/checkpoints) is not, so there is no way to synthesize a genuinely AI-generated bitmap from a text prompt without a tool or network call that this runtime does not provide. Producing a placeholder image via PIL/ImageMagick primitives would not be the skill's actual deliverable (an AI-generated image) and was intentionally not substituted.
tools_used: python3 -c (import checks: torch, diffusers, openai, PIL)
evidence: Ran in work dir: python3 -c 'import diffusers' -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'diffusers'. python3 -c 'import openai' -> succeeded (package present, version 3.19.2) but no OPENAI_API_KEY set (checked `${OPENAI_API_KEY:+yes}` -> empty) and no network access is available per the runtime's stated constraints, so the openai client cannot be used to reach the Images API. `which convert magick gimp inkscape` returned nothing (no alternative raster tools that do AI generation). `pip list | grep -iE 'diffus|torch|openai|pillow|stable'` showed only openai, pillow, and torch present -- no diffusers/stable-diffusion package or local model weights that would allow offline text-to-image synthesis. Conclusion: neither of the skill's two supported modes (built-in tool; CLI+API) can be exercised in this offline, tool-less-for-imagegen runtime, and no substitute local generative model is installed, so the core deliverable (an actual generated image) could not be produced or verified.
